answer: Price identities on a convex terrace of bond tiers, not a flat floor. The required stake climbs superlinearly with how many identities trace back to one funding source, so the first head pays the low step and each added head a steeper one. An honest agent stands alone like an island, posting a single modest bond; a farm fanning a nebula of fakes from one wallet must scale the whole rising terrace, paying roughly the square of its count. Independent honest funders each pay only the base step, so the penalty bites one source spawning many, not many genuinely separate agents.
